practiceSet.title: U4.LT3 Practice: Acceleration
practiceSet.description: Practice identifying acceleration and calculating acceleration, final velocity, and time, including slowing down and unit conversions.

activity.title: U4.LT3 Relearning: Acceleration
activity.content:
**What you need to be able to do:** I can identify and calculate acceleration.

**Think about riding in a car.** You feel pushed back into your seat when the driver steps on the gas, you lean forward when the driver brakes, and you slide sideways when the car turns a corner. Each of those pushes is your body noticing that the velocity changed. When the car cruises straight down the highway at a steady speed, you feel nothing, even at 65 mph. That feeling of change is acceleration.

**Acceleration** is the rate of change of velocity. When the velocity of an object changes, the object is accelerating. Because velocity is speed and direction, there are **three ways to accelerate**: **speeding up**, **slowing down**, and **changing direction**. A car going around a curve at a constant speed is still accelerating, because its direction changes. **Zero acceleration** means constant speed in a straight line.

**Formula:** a = (v_{f} − v_{i}) / t, where v_{f} is final velocity, v_{i} is initial velocity, and t is time. "From rest" means v_{i} = 0. To find final velocity: v_{f} = v_{i} + a × t. To find time: t = (v_{f} − v_{i}) / a.

**Units:** the SI unit is **m/s^{2}**. It comes from (m/s) / s: a change in velocity (m/s) divided by time (s). 3 m/s^{2} means the velocity changes by 3 m/s every second. If speeds are in km/h and time is in seconds, the unit is km/h/s.

**Negative acceleration (deceleration):** for an object moving forward, positive = speeding up and negative = slowing down. Always do final minus initial and keep the sign.

**Worked example 1:** A bike speeds up from 4 m/s to 10 m/s in 3 s. Formula: a = (v_{f} − v_{i}) / t. Set Up: a = (10 m/s − 4 m/s) / 3 s = 6 m/s / 3 s. Answer: 2 m/s^{2}.

**Worked example 2:** A skateboarder is traveling 12 m/s, crashes, and slides to a stop in 2 s. Formula: a = (v_{f} − v_{i}) / t. Set Up: a = (0 m/s − 12 m/s) / 2 s. Answer: -6 m/s^{2} (negative because he is slowing down).

**Worked example 3:** A car moving forward at 20 m/s has an acceleration of −4.0 m/s^{2}. What is its velocity after 3 s? Formula: v_{f} = v_{i} + a × t. Set Up: v_{f} = 20 m/s + (−4.0 m/s^{2} × 3 s) = 20 m/s − 12 m/s. Answer: 8 m/s forward.

**Watch out for:** forgetting that turning counts as acceleration, subtracting backwards (v_{i} − v_{f}) and getting the wrong sign, leaving off the units (m/s^{2}, not m/s), and mixing hours, minutes, and seconds. If a speed is in mph or km/h and the answer needs m/s^{2}, convert to m/s first.
prompts: Name the three ways an object can accelerate and give a real example of each.
A dog runs from rest to 9 m/s in 3 s. Find its acceleration using Formula / Set Up / Answer with units.
A car has an acceleration of 6 m/s^{2}. How much time is needed for it to reach 18 m/s from rest? Show your setup.
Explain why a car on a straight road at a constant 100 km/h has zero acceleration, but a car going around a curve at 35 mi/h does not.
